title: Mount a power supply with its required cooling gap
instruction: Mount the white power supply on the DIN rail to the right of the grey modules. Its datasheet requires 20 to 30 mm of free air between it and the module beside it for cooling, so leave a gap of that size.
context: DIN-rail power supplies cool by convection, and their datasheets specify side clearances; mounted flush against a neighbour they overheat and derate, while too large a gap wastes rail space needed for the next device. The placement therefore has a numeric window rather than a target point. Unlike TK-7FTC8C (snap a module onto an empty rail), the target is a numeric window from a datasheet rule rather than a single seated position. Done by: electricians and electrical equipment assemblers (O*NET 47-2111.00, 51-2022.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table. Rail: a steel TS35 x 7.5 DIN rail lying flat, 3.5 cm wide, 30 cm long, 0.75 cm tall, along y, centred at x 30, y 27, fixed. On it, all fixed: a dark steel end clamp (4 x 1 x 3 cm) centred at y 40.5; three grey I/O modules (8 cm across the rail, 4.5 cm wide, 6 cm tall) packed against it, centred at y 37.75, 33.25 and 28.75 (the last one's right face at y 26.5); a second end clamp centred at y 13.5. Power supply: a white box 8 cm deep (x), 6 cm wide (y), 7 cm tall, 400 g, standing on the table at x 16, y 25.
scoring: From a top photo and a ruler, with the grippers open. 0.25 once the supply is at least 3 cm above the table. 0.5 when it is seated on the rail: bottom within 2 mm of the rail top, centred across the rail within 4 mm, square and upright within 4 degrees, still. When seated, the gap is the free air between its left face and the last module's right face: 1.0 for 20 to 30 mm, 0.75 for 10 to 20 mm or 30 to 40 mm, 0.5 otherwise (touching, or more than 40 mm). Success: seated with 20 to 30 mm, held 1 s.
reset_notes: Stand the supply back on its mark on the table.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The rail lies flat on the table instead of on an upright panel, its profile is a solid bar, and the modules and clamps are fixed. The supply has no DIN clip: it rests on the rail by gravity and goes straight on, where a real one hooks on and snaps.
